payload.title: Shared log: ledger audit omits claim conflicts; conflict detection can be spurious
payload.body: FEAT-694 review. (1) LedgerService._shared_log_audit (ledger/service.py) does not report claim conflicts; they exist only in the transient SharedLogImportReport and are lost when hooks redirect output to /dev/null (AC10 partly met). (2) import_shared_log's claim-conflict loop compares imported issue.claimed payloads with the final claimed_by, so history 'A claims, A unclaims, B claims' yields a bogus A-vs-B conflict. Fix: flag only claims that lost / ignore claims superseded by later unclaimed/closed; persist or recompute conflicts statelessly for audit; add an audit test.

payload.title: shared_log.py hardening: rotation dup on crash, unknown kinds, trailing newline, path digest, archive-only pre-import
payload.body: FEAT-694 review suggestions, all in ledger/shared_log.py unless noted: rotate_events appends to archives before os.replace of current, so a crash duplicates lines (skip event_ids already in archive); rotation moves every non-issue.* event, spec says only task.*/spec.*/insight.*; export_events appends without ensuring existing file ends in newline; digest_files/_stable_relative_path key off first 'sdd' path component (use relative_to(repo_root)); LedgerService.claim pre-import checks only events.jsonl existence, should use shared_log_files(); cli.py --stage subprocess check=True CalledProcessError uncaught; spec §1 lacks explicit 'superseded by FEAT-694' marker for the FEAT-671 non-goal (AC13).

payload.title: test_report CLI can exit non-zero / skip output, contradicting "never blocks" in /sdd-done §4.7
payload.body: scripts/sdd/test_report.py main() returns 2 on an unreadable index or bad args and prints nothing; args.out.write_text is unguarded (OSError -> exit 1). With an empty DECISION and no $TEST_REPORT_MD, `gh pr create --body-file "$TEST_REPORT_MD"` in the hotfix/fallback commands fails on a missing file. Fix: on an unusable index emit a minimal "## Tests — no data" section and return 0; catch OSError on --out; guard --body-file in the .md text.

payload.title: Test report table hides count-less failures (timed_out/no_junit/parse_error) and discards corrupt-record notes
payload.body: report.py render_markdown marks ❌ only when failed+errors>0, so a timed_out/no_junit/report_parse_error suite renders as 0/0 and reads as "nothing ran". The per-task <details> shows only suite count and attempts. test_report.py render discards load_records notes (corrupt files) though the spec says they are reported. Also suggestions: append_suite overwrites record-level head_sha/tier/source on every append (per-suite head_sha would make AC5 stale marking accurate); the _rerun record is not checked for staleness against the final HEAD.

payload.reason: Amended TASK-4411/4414 blueprints: render_markdown ❌ now triggers on status!=ok (covers timed_out/no_junit/report_parse_error), added notes parameter for corrupt-record notes, documented append_suite last-write-wins, added rerun staleness check. PR #1708.

payload.title: Review TASK-4421
jira_cli auth accepts a bare pasted code without any state/CSRF check
payload.body: packages/ai-parrot-tools/src/parrot_tools/jira_cli.py (auth command, ~lines 288-292): a pasted full redirect URL is state-checked with hmac.compare_digest, but a bare code only logs a warning and proceeds, so a stripped-down paste bypasses the CSRF check. Spec AC3 says a state mismatch aborts. Suggested fix: require the full redirect URL, or gate bare codes behind an explicit --allow-bare-code flag. Found by the FEAT-696 independent review.

payload.title: FEAT-696 AC7: KB issue-type/project resolution only wired into jira_get_create_fields, not jira_create_issue
payload.body: packages/ai-parrot-tools/src/parrot_tools/jiratoolkit.py: jira_create_issue only calls KB validate_limits/resolve_field; it has no issue-type/project lookup that the KB could short-circuit, so 'no lookup call' (AC7) holds trivially and the 'jira KB stale' log is emitted only from jira_get_create_fields, jira_get_issue_types and the components lookup. Confirm the intended behaviour with the spec owner and add a test that matches the AC7 wording (create_issue with a known issue type makes no lookup call; unknown type triggers a live lookup and logs 'jira KB stale').

payload.title: jira OAuth helpers echo raw response bodies into exceptions/CLI output; local token store crashes on corrupt JSON
payload.body: parrot/auth/jira_oauth.py helpers (exchange_code, refresh_access_token, fetch_accessible_resources, fetch_myself) put the raw response text into ValueError; parrot_tools/jira_cli.py (_load_fresh_token ~252, status probe ~355) echoes it. Truncate/sanitize. Also LocalJiraTokenStore.load()/get() (jira_local_auth.py ~63-78) raise an unhandled JSONDecodeError on a corrupt settings file instead of a clean 're-authenticate' error, and jira_cli exposes --client-secret on argv (shell history); consider dropping the flag in favour of the hidden prompt/env. Found by the FEAT-696 independent review.

payload.body: packages/ai-parrot/tests/cli/tui/test_widgets.py::test_composer_enter_submits_and_ctrl_j_newline hangs under the sandboxed runner (reproduced on dev: killed after 60s). Also ~75 failures in the ai-parrot jira-scope set (test_jira_*.py, test_jiratoolkit_*.py) and ~144 failures/33 errors in ai-parrot-tools merge-tier exist on dev. payload.title: sdd-coder blast-radius collector always exits 1 in worktrees (no wiki plane) — contract-symbol tasks forced to strong seats
payload.body: _collect_wiki_blast (complexity_collectors.py:643-666) runs `python -m parrot.knowledge.wiki.cli symbols blast --path <worktree> ...` with cwd=worktree. A feature worktree has no `.parrot/wiki` plane (it lives only in the main checkout), so the CLI exits 1 with "Wiki not built yet for <path>. Run `wikitoolkit build` first." — reproduced 2026-10-17 by running the exact command against a path without a wiki plane. The collector records `blast_symbols` state=unknown ("Blast radius incomplete (sym:...: exit 1)"), and ComplexityPolicy routes `unknown` like `complex` (strong_models allowlist only, commit 957c15d96). Net effect measured in artifacts/logs/sdd-coder-usage: October 2026 has 93 unknown + 186 complex vs 26 standard assessments — ~91% of tasks bypass the cheap seats (nova glm/minimax/qwen/mistral, gemini, codex-spark, haiku) and land on gpt-5.6-terra / native sonnet. Every task that declares Codebase Contract symbols is systematically classified unknown. Fix direction: resolve the wiki plane from the main checkout (git rev-parse --git-common-dir parent, same pattern as telemetry.resolve_durable_root) instead of the worktree path, or fall back to the main-checkout plane when the worktree has none; symbols genuinely missing from the plane should still yield missing-root unknown, but plane-absent must not.

payload.title: sdd_coder MCP surface rejects HOTFIX-<KEY>-N brief task ids
payload.body: Brief tasks use ids HOTFIX-<KEY>-N, but sdd_coder hard-codes ^TASK-\d{1,5}$: sdd_coder/models.py:110 (_check_task_id, used at ~598/608/752/783), optimization_models.py:31 and :209, background.py:69 and :544 (coder_run_validation), plus test_scope/report.py:75 _SAFE_ID_RE. Any coder_* call with a HOTFIX id fails validation, so --split briefs cannot use the MCP coder path (only single-agent/manual). _FEATURE_ID_RE was widened to BRIEF-* in FEAT-698 but task-id regexes were not. Fix: widen to ^(TASK-\d{1,5}|HOTFIX-[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*-\d{1,5})$ in those places with tests that call a request model with a HOTFIX id.

payload.title: brief_meta/ensure_worktree: weak ref validation (.. / .lock) and base_branch not checked
payload.body: scripts/sdd/brief_meta.py _SAFE_REF_RE permits '..', trailing '.' and '.lock' (invalid git ref components) so a bad key fails inside git worktree add rather than at parse time. brief_worktree_plan / ensure_worktree --brief-key do not validate base_branch against {main,dev,staging} nor enforce ledger=>dev (only BriefMeta does). Also ResearchOutput.index_path is str default '' vs spec Optional[str]=None (acceptable, noted). Also the .agent/skills/worktree-management twin still carries old 'opens a PR feature -> base_branch' wording (TASK-4437 deviation).

payload.reason: Hardened brief ref validation (_is_safe_ref rejects '..', trailing '.', '.lock') and added BRIEF_BASE_BRANCHES {main,dev,staging} enforced in BriefMeta and brief_worktree_plan, so ensure_worktree --brief-key validates at parse time. Also aligned the .agent worktree-management twin (TASK-4437 deviation). ledger=>dev stays a BriefMeta invariant: source type is not derivable in the planner.
